channel.title: Crypto Docket
channel.description: Crypto Docket reports news across crypto: Bitcoin and Ethereum, layer-2 networks, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Fairshake backs 32 House candidates as crypto bill stalls
item.description: Fairshake named 32 House candidates for midterm support, including six $1 million commitments, as its preferred market-structure bill remains stalled in the Senate.

item.title: Moving Polygon Proceeds to an Ethereum Exchange
item.description: Moving Polygon proceeds to an Ethereum-only exchange means bridging to a wallet you control, claiming on Ethereum, then depositing the matching asset.

item.title: Bitget breach exposes risk beyond stolen private keys
item.description: Bitget says attackers stole $387.5 million from hot and warm wallets through forged withdrawals; phased services have resumed, but the breach reached beyond private keys.

item.title: Convert Payroll Reserves Into Tokens With the Ledger Intact
item.description: Turning payroll reserves into tokens adds conversion and settlement steps; a workable setup keeps wage amounts, tax withholding, liquidity and wallet delivery auditable.

item.title: When Impermanent Loss Outruns Fees in a Liquidity Pool
item.description: LP fees can offset the cost of a changing token mix, but only when active trading earns enough; compare both sides with holding before judging returns.

item.title: A USDT Swap on TRON Needs TRX Left for Network Fees
item.description: A USDT swap on TRON can spend TRX on contract fees as well as the trade, so check the quoted cost, any approval step and your remaining balance.

item.title: For a TRON Swap, the Wallet Network Sets the Route
item.description: A TRON swap works only when the wallet, token and destination use the same chain; compare fees, liquidity and bridge risk before choosing a network.

item.title: Failed BNB Chain Swaps Have No Fixed Volume Discount
item.description: Failed BNB Chain swaps do not create a fixed volume drop: the size depends on which trades fail, retry, or disappear from the measured window.

item.title: Inventory-backed swaps move MEV from pools to quotes
item.description: Inventory-backed swaps trade against a market maker’s tokens instead of a pool, changing price impact and MEV exposure while shifting risk to the quote and its provider.

item.title: When LP Fees Outrun Impermanent Loss
item.description: LP fees cover impermanent loss only when your position earns more than its value gap versus holding; compare both over the same period and price path.

item.title: A cross-chain swap needs a way back
item.description: Cross-chain swaps need defined paths for timeouts, retries and refunds because a failure on the destination chain can leave source funds committed without a usable trade.

item.title: USDT on Manta: choose the route by token and exit
item.description: The right USDT route to Manta depends on the exact token you need, the exit path and gas; compare native settlement with third-party routes before signing.

item.title: Base token approvals: cap the permission before you trade
item.description: On Base, a token approval is a standing permission: set it to the amount needed, check the spender, and revisit it when the transaction is done.

item.title: SEC proposes crypto custody routes for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed crypto custody rules for advisers and regulated funds, opening conditional self-custody and state trust company routes where existing rules leave few workable options.

item.title: A Treasury Transfer Schedule Needs More Than a Send Time
item.description: A cross-chain treasury schedule is a policy and execution loop, not a timed bridge button: separate the trigger, source submission and destination settlement.

item.title: Solana swap costs: compare the full trade, not just the fee
item.description: Solana swap costs include more than the network fee. Compare quoted output, pool charges, price impact and setup costs for the same trade.

item.title: A Token Symbol Is a Label, Not an Identity
item.description: A token symbol is a label, not an identity; network and contract address reveal whether lookalikes are the same asset, a bridged copy or unrelated tokens on different chains.

item.title: Tether-backed Utexo plans USDT’s return to Bitcoin via RGB
item.description: Tether-backed Utexo plans to issue USDT on Bitcoin through RGB this month, adding private transfers and BTC swaps while shifting transaction data off the public ledger.

item.title: How Ethereum Deposits Become Polygon Credits
item.description: Polygon’s PoS bridge locks tokens on Ethereum and issues mapped credits on Polygon, trading a single-chain balance for a two-chain claim and exit process.

item.title: fermi swap vs AMM routes: the wallet integration trade-off
item.description: Fermi swap gives wallet users a direct token-exchange option, while AMM routing can compare pools; the choice shifts control, complexity and execution.
